verdict.rationale: Installed plugins and skills are used inside ChatGPT and Codex chats. Codex picks a skill from its name and description and loads it when relevant, or the user can name it in plain language ("use the PR skill to open a PR"); plugins like Slack then summarize channels or draft replies on request. Plugin management itself mostly relies on slash commands, `$`/`@` mentions and CLI subcommands rather than free-form natural language. missing for 10: documented natural-language control of plugin install and management, first-party docs showing conversational invocation end-to-end, and hands-on corroboration of how reliably Codex chooses a skill from a natural-language request.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: After installation, you can use plugins in Chat or Work in ChatGPT, or in Codex.
ChatGPT and Codex start with each skill's name and description, then load the full `SKILL.md` instructions when they decide to use that skill.
Install the Slack plugin to summarize channels or draft replies.
You can also invoke them explicitly, e.g. "use the PR skill to open a PR."
